notes: None of the nine listed rules changed since db91c23: `git diff db91c23 -- idiomatic-elixir/` touches only SKILL.md's with rule (a new sentence on a one-step with in a public function), the new rule "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else", the captures rule, and testing.md's "Assert with patterns". All nine are graded to the 2026-10-22 standard: an option value (:base_url, :timeout, :req_options, the API key) passed to Req unchecked violates Make polymorphism explicit; `## Options` in the @moduledoc instead of new/1's @doc counts against Group related parameters; an API key held in a Req request inside a package struct with no Inspect handling is violated, and a key never stored in a package struct is not exercised; config read inside a function at call time is clean for Read configuration at runtime; a message/1 under @impl needs no @spec.

Two tier results differ from the 2026-10-22 baseline sweep because the runs differ, not the rules. Opus-1 this time keeps the key inside a Req request in its struct with no Inspect derive (line 18, line 56) and checks only the key among the option values (lines 49, 55-59), so Opus is violated for Keep secrets out of logs and inspect output and Make polymorphism explicit (both clean last sweep). Both Sonnet runs take every setting as a new/1 option with no Application call, so Sonnet is clean for Take configuration as arguments (violated last sweep).

Rules outside the list that changed since db91c23 were checked for other_violations. "Use `do:` for a one-expression body and `do ... end` for anything else" is new; its sentence "A one-expression body too long for the head's line wants a block or a helper" applies to sonnet-1's message/1 clauses (lines 118-122), which wrap the body onto a `, do:` line. The one-step with sentence "When the body of a one-step `with` calls another function that can fail, that call is the second step" (unchanged) applies to haiku-1 line 72; no run has a one-step with in the shape the new sentence adds. No capture in any run is affected by the captures change. Other other_violations follow the previous standard (`unless`, a pipeline that starts with a call, a catch-all that reports a bad key as missing, a value-checking `fetch_*`, unformatted lines).

format_ok in result.json was confirmed with mix format --check-formatted on copies: haiku-1 passes; opus-1 (lines 125, 167), haiku-2 (line 87), sonnet-1 (lines 68, 77) and sonnet-2 (lines 65, 74) fail.

Compile results come from result.json. Four of five files do not compile for a reason unrelated to Req: a module builds a struct (%Error{} or %Forecast{}) of a module the same file defines later. Haiku-2 compiles, with warnings only for the absent Req. These are noted in the summaries, as the 2026-10-22 grades did.

Expected reads (library-design.md) is unmet in every run, as expected for baseline: reads is empty in all five, and the transcripts show no Skill or Read call, only Write (and one mkdir in haiku-1). All five have rc 0, and each transcript's assistant messages report the model_id of its tier.
